D013-D009_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling so heavy these past five months—everything just takes too much effort. Some days, getting out of bed feels impossible. I move slower, picking up even a cup feels like lifting a stone. I cry a lot, sometimes for no reason, other times thinking about how I wasn’t there enough for my husband before he passed, or how I burned that one meal at work last month. Those little things loop in my head, over and over. I keep thinking I’ve failed—my family, my job.  

At work, I used to be quick, but now I’m behind. My supervisor noticed. I’ve even had these sudden urges—like standing near the stairs at the building where I clean, and just… wondering what it’d be like to step off. Not that I’d do it, but the thought just pops in.  

There were short bursts—maybe a week or two—where I felt unusually wired, cleaned for hours without tiring, needed less sleep, my mind racing. But it never lasted. It didn’t feel like mania, just... off. And then I’d crash again. I can’t say if it meant anything. Maybe I’m just worn out.

    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
